Incorporates reversible terminator nucleotides followed by imaging and deprotection
Focuses on identifying regions of genomic differences and SNPs
Focuses on sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators
Used to detect SNPs in different genomic regions
Used for high throughput, accurate sequencing without gel electrophoresis

shortQuestions.question: List the main file formats used in Bioinformatics mentioned in the lesson.
Briefly explain why it is essential to recognize different bioinformatics file formats.

answerBlocks.text: Different software packages usually accept only specific file formats, and different databases hold information in different formats. Therefore, recognizing and interconverting between these formats is an essential skill for analysis.

shortQuestions.question: What is the SRA format and what type of data does it require?

answerBlocks.text: The SRA (Sequence Read Archive) is a "raw data" archive that requires per-base quality scores for all submitted data.

shortQuestions.question: Why are FASTA and other sequence-only formats not sufficient for SRA submission?

answerBlocks.text: Because SRA requires per-base quality scores, sequence-only formats like FASTA do not provide this information and thus are not sufficient for submission.

shortQuestions.question: Which file formats does SRA prefer for submission?
Can FASTA files be submitted to SRA? If yes, under what conditions?

answerBlocks.text: FASTA files can be submitted as reference sequences for BAM files or as part of a FASTA/QUAL pair, but not as the main raw data submission.

shortQuestions.question: Define BAM files in the context of NGS data formats.

answerBlocks.text: **BAM files** are binary alignment/map files which are the preferred format for SRA submissions. They are compressed versions of the Sequence Alignment/Map (SAM) format and can be decompressed back to the human-readable SAM text format using specific utilities.

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain the SAM file format.

answerBlocks.text: SAM (Sequence Alignment Map) format is a TAB-delimited text format used to store alignment data. It consists of a header section where each line starts with '@' and an alignment body section where each line contains alignment information without '@'.

shortQuestions.question: List the 11 compulsory fields present in each alignment line of a SAM file.

items: Chromosome/contig which read pair aligned to
Position which read pair aligned to

shortQuestions.question: Distinguish between SAM and BAM file formats.

items: SAM is a text-based format storing alignment data, while BAM is the binary version of SAM.
BAM files are compressed and preferred for storage and submission, whereas SAM files are human-readable.
SAM files can be converted to BAM and vice versa using SAM tools utilities.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the significance of the SAM flag in a SAM file.

answerBlocks.text: The SAM flag is a compulsory field in the SAM alignment line that contains aligner-specific information used to describe properties of the read and its alignment, such as whether the read is paired, mapped, or a duplicate.

shortQuestions.question: Explain how SAM tools utility is used in relation to SAM and BAM files.

answerBlocks.text: SAM tools is a utility software that can convert files between SAM (text) and BAM (binary) formats, allowing users to compress or decompress alignment data as needed.

shortQuestions.question: Define the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO).

answerBlocks.text: The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) is a public repository for the archiving and distribution of gene expression data submitted by the scientific community.

shortQuestions.question: List the four kinds of data records in GEO architecture.

items: Platform (GPL) - the technology used and the features detected
Sample (GSM) - preparation and description of the sample
Series (GSE) - defines a set of samples and how they are related
Datasets (GDS) - sample data collections assembled by GEO staff

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain what MIAME compliance means in the context of GEO.

answerBlocks.text: MIAME compliance refers to the Minimum Information About a Microarray Experiment, which is a standard ensuring that sufficient information about a microarray experiment is provided for interpretation and reproducibility.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the types of raw data submitters may provide to GEO.
Distinguish between Platform (GPL) and Sample (GSM) data records in GEO.

answerBlocks.text: Platform (GPL) records describe the technology used and the features detected on a given platform.
Sample (GSM) records describe the preparation and details of the biological sample used in the experiment.

shortQuestions.question: Explain how GEO data can be accessed using accession numbers from scientific papers.

answerBlocks.text: GEO data can be accessed by using accession numbers provided in scientific papers, which often include hyperlinks to the GEO accession page or can be entered manually into the GEO home page query box.

lessons.title: Module162: Lesson-10- SRA Files and SRA File Handling & SAM File

shortQuestions.question: Define Sequence Read Archive (SRA) files.

answerBlocks.text: Sequence Read Archive (SRA) files are a common format used by the NCBI, EBI, and others for storing reads and read alignments. They provide good compression and data accessibility but often require transformation for visualization and analytical processing.

shortQuestions.question: List the goals of the SRA data submission guide.

items: Specify which data formats are currently supported by SRA.
Enable submitters to validate and convert data prior to submission to avoid unnecessary data transfers.
Improve the speed of submission processing.
Reduce the probability of failed submissions.
Improve other services provided by SRA by freeing up time previously spent to correct and transform data.

shortQuestions.question: Explain why FASTA format alone is not sufficient for SRA submissions.

answerBlocks.text: The SRA is a “raw data” archive and requires per-base quality scores for all submitted data. FASTA and other sequence-only formats lack these quality scores and thus are not sufficient for submission. However, FASTA can be submitted as reference sequences for BAM files.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the advantages of using container files in SRA submissions.

items: All data for a given library is contained in one file.
Data are indexed for random access.
Data are compressed so gzip and other compression utilities are discouraged.
Data are streamable (can be read from one input handle).
Data are self-identifying (file type can be interrogated with file).

shortQuestions.question: Distinguish between the SRA data model before and after its transition.

answerBlocks.text: Previously, the SRA data model consisted of “dumps” of whole flowcell lanes or production runs. After transition, it became a semi-curated database of sample-specific sequencing libraries.

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain how to install the SRA toolkit on Linux.

items: Download the toolkit using wget from the NCBI FTP site.
Unpack the downloaded tar.gz file using the command: tar -xzf sratoolkit.current-centos_linux64.tar.gz.
Navigate to the sra-toolkit folder to access executables like fastq-dump.

shortQuestions.question: List the functions of the following SRA toolkit tools: fastq-dump, sam-dump, and sff-dump.

rows: fastq-dump
Converts data to FASTq and FASTA format.
sam-dump
Converts data to SAM (human-readable BAM). Aligned BAM data output as aligned SAM; others as unaligned SAM.
sff-dump
Converts data to SFF format; only data submitted as SFF can be converted back.

shortQuestions.question: What additional information do SRA container files include besides the sequencing data?

answerBlocks.text: SRA container files include run-time configuration and execution parameters such as run date, instrument name, flow cell name, processing program, and version.

shortQuestions.question: Explain the purpose of the vdb-dump tool in the SRA toolkit.

answerBlocks.text: The vdb-dump tool exports the vdb-formatted data of the .sra file.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the steps to run fastq-dump on Linux to extract 5 reads from an SRA file.

items: Open a terminal and change directory to the folder containing the SRA toolkit executables.
Run the command: ./fastq-dump -X 5 -Z SRR390728 to extract 5 reads.

shortQuestions.question: Define the term 'Template' in NGS analysis.

answerBlocks.text: A Template is a DNA/RNA sequence part of which is sequenced on a sequencing machine or assembled from raw sequences.

shortQuestions.question: What is a 'Segment' in the context of NGS data?

answerBlocks.text: A Segment is a contiguous sequence or subsequence.

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain what a 'Read' is in NGS sequencing.

answerBlocks.text: A Read is a raw sequence that comes off a sequencing machine. It may consist of multiple segments and is indexed by the order in which it is sequenced.

items: Range of a read varies from 90 bp to 180 bp and can be up to 1000 bp depending on the sequencing machine used.

shortQuestions.question: Distinguish between 'Chimeric alignment' and 'Read alignment'.

answerBlocks.text: Chimeric alignment is an alignment of a read that cannot be represented as a linear alignment and is represented as a set of linear alignments without large overlaps.
Read alignment refers to either a linear alignment or a chimeric alignment that completely represents the alignment of the read.

shortQuestions.question: What is meant by 'Multiple mapping' in NGS read alignment?

answerBlocks.text: Multiple mapping occurs when the correct placement of a read is ambiguous, often due to repeats, resulting in multiple read alignments for the same read.
One alignment is considered primary, while others have the secondary alignment flag set.

shortQuestions.question: List the flags used in SAM records to distinguish different types of alignments in chimeric and multiple mapping cases.

items: Supplementary alignment flag: used to distinguish supplementary alignments in chimeric alignment.
Secondary alignment flag: used for alignments other than the primary in multiple mapping.
Flags 0x40 and 0x80: same values for all SAM records with the same QNAME in chimeric and multiple mapping alignments.
